synopsis: The booklet recommends a restricted first release that widens only through evidence gates; all off-road collision-intervention products found in the research launched with narrow operating domains [f73, f379, f608, f11941]. The proposed initial envelope is reverse-only, low-speed braking on selected machine models, subject to a closed safety case; expert judgment additionally recommends a brief brake pulse returning control to the operator and exclusions for stockpiles, trailer loading and slopes [f721, f10972, f1597]. Volvo CE’s January 2023 precedent operated only in reverse at 3–15 km/h, and industry scope limits reflect hazards discovered through field experience [f420, f10640]. Narrowing the envelope reduces validation burden and can shorten time to a bounded release, but it does not validate excluded conditions; staged release requires runtime domain monitoring, a field-data loop and regulatory acceptance [f1599, f615, f616]. Field operation should begin without brake authority, warning-only behavior should remain outside the released envelope, and operator behavior change requires staged release with field monitoring [f752, f10975, f11859]. The proposed G4 release gate is August–September 2027, with release, restricted release or withholding determined by evidence supporting explicitly bounded claims; a funded restricted-scope fallback is recommended alongside virtual-validation development [f12308, f10747].
